sam-cust: Hey — hitting a production failure where a streaming tool-call returns a schema_error. The model starts a tool call but the JSON args are cut mid-object. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Happened ~10:23:44 UTC.

sam-cust: Quick excerpt from client raw stream (SSE):

```
event: message
data: {\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":100,\"currency\":\"USD\"\

event: message
data: \\"[TRUNCATED]\"```

sam-cust: Parser fails because the JSON payload never gets the closing braces. We only see partial chunk. Happening on Node fetch and our Python consumer.

alex-support: Thanks @sam-cust. Can you attach the full client log (hex/bytes around the boundary) and confirm if you're using any proxy or CDN in front of the service? Also which SDK (node/py) and model + route?

sam-cust: We're on node-fetch v3, using the hosted API -> model=gpt-4o-infer. Our infra sits behind CloudFront (for edge) then ALB -> NGINX proxy -> service. I'll paste the last bytes: 

```
... 0a 7b 22 74 79 70 65 22 3a 22 74 6f 6f 6c 5f 63 61 6c 6c 22 2c 22 6e 61 6d 65 22 3a 22 63 68 61 72 67 65 22 2c 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 7b 22 61 6d 6f 75 6e 74 22 3a 31 30 30 2c 22 63 75 72 72 65 6e 63 79 22 3a 22 55 53 44
```

sam-cust: ends exactly at the D, no 22 7d 7d (\"})

maria-eng: This matches other reports where the SSE \"data:\" payload is split mid-json token by an intermediate buffer/flush boundary. Common culprits: proxy/nginx buffering + gzip flush, or ALB chunking behavior. Two quick notes:
1) Streaming endpoints must make sure each SSE \"data\" chunk carries a complete JSON message. If the runtime writes a large JSON across multiple res.write() calls, intermediaries can split.
2) Some CDNs/ALBs will split/merge TCP frames unpredictably; clients should be resilient by concatenating received bytes until a parsable JSON object is formed.

maria-eng: Repro snippet you can run locally to simulate chunked writes (node):

```
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
  res.write('event: message\n');
  // write JSON in two partial writes to simulate the bug
  res.write('data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"charge","args":{"amount":100,');
  setTimeout(() => {
    res.write('"currency":"USD"}}\n\n');
    res.end();
  }, 50);
}).listen(8080);
```

maria-eng: If a proxy between client and server buffers and flushes differently, the client can see the second write as a separate SSE event or lose the boundary.

tony-sre: Correlation req_0a1b2c3d shows Gateway logs with a 200 streaming response but our ALB logs show several TCP FIN/FIN_WAIT entries around 10:23:45. Also saw gzip on the route. My hunch: gzip + chunked transfer + proxy_buffering ON on nginx results in boundary reflow.

maria-eng: Quick mitigations for customers:
- Client-side: accumulate SSE data frames until JSON.parse succeeds; don't assume one SSE == one JSON.
- Server-side (recommended): ensure you flush only after a complete JSON object, or wrap tool args in a single field (e.g., base64) to avoid mid-token splits, or send each tool-call as a single SSE message with a final newline-separated terminator.
- Infra change: on nginx set `proxy_buffering off` for SSE endpoints and add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` upstream. Also consider disabling gzip for SSE endpoints (`gzip off`).

sam-cust: Ok we'll implement client concat parsing as a short-term fix. Can you confirm this is not a bug in the SDK? We're using the official node SDK streaming helpers.

alex-support: @maria-eng, any SDK mitigations we can offer so customers don't need to implement lower-level parsing? Could the SDK reassemble partial events automatically?

maria-eng: Yes, SDK can do that: the streaming helper should treat stream as a byte stream and buffer until it can parse a full JSON object or until a message delimiter (we prefer explicit delimiting). I'll open an SDK PR to: 1) buffer and attempt incremental JSON repairs (concatenate & try parse repeatedly), 2) emit a stream-level `incomplete_toolcall` debug event with raw bytes when parse fails, and 3) expose a `sseAllowPartial` flag for advanced users.

tony-sre: On infra side, I'll add a temporary rule on the ALB -> NGINX path to disable gzip and set `proxy_buffering off` for `/v1/stream/*` routes to validate if behavior changes for the customer's traffic. I'll post results in ~30m.

deploy-bot: deploy started by tony-sre: disable-gzip-sse-test (canary) -> 3/3 hosts.

sam-cust: Thanks, I tested with a quick client concat fix and the parser now succeeds for the previously failing message. Will keep you posted if anything else crops up.

alex-support: Filing an internal escalation ticket: #INC-6821 with repro, traces, and suggested mitigations. Assigning to @maria-eng for SDK fix and @tony-sre for infra validation.

maria-eng: I'll follow up with a small SDK patch and a note in docs recommending SSE framing rules. Proposed short-term server change: always send complete tool args in one write or base64-wrap args to force single-token boundaries.

sam-cust: Appreciate the quick response. Workaround in place, will monitor. :thumbsup:

alex-support: Marking thread as resolved for now, reopening if customer sees recurrence.
